queue.title: Iran flogs female singer 74 times for performing without hijab in viral YouTube concert
queue.dek: Lawyers said singer Parastoo Ahmadi and members of her concert team received 74 lashes each in Qom after performing without a hijab. They also face two-year bans.
queue.opening: Iranian authorities subjected a female singer and four members of her concert team to 74 lashes each Monday after she defied the Islamic Republic’s restrictions on women by performing without a hijab in a viral YouTube concert, their lawyers said. Parastoo Ahmadi, 29, and her four male co-defendants were flogged in the Iranian city of Qom, defense attorney Mostafa Nili told Iranian news outlet Emtedad, according to Reuters. The five were also banned from traveling abroad and engaging in artistic and musical activities for two years. IRAN'S REGIME CAME FOR TEENAGE TWINS. THEIR FATE OFFERS A GLIMPSE OF TEHRAN'S WIDENING DEATH CAMPAIGN One of the defendants’ lawyers told the BBC Monday that efforts to overturn the ruling, reduce the punishment or suspend its enforcement had failed. Defense attorneys also sought to postpone the flogging, but authorities insisted on carrying out the sentence immediately. The punishment sparked outrage among Iranian artists and human rights advocates , who condemned the regime’s restrictions on women and artistic expression. Bahar Ghandehari, director of advocacy at the U.S.-based Center for Human Rights in Iran (CHRI), told the BBC that Ahmadi’s flogging was "a flagrant violation of her fundamental rights" and demonstrated the authorities’ determination to suppress women’s freedoms and punish those who challenge discriminatory laws. queue.opening: President Donald Trump will award former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani the Presidential Medal of Freedom on Tuesday during a closed-press ceremony at the White House, honoring the longtime prosecutor and "America's Mayor" for his lifetime of public service. The Presidential Medal of Freedom is the nation's highest civilian honor, alongside the Congressional Gold Medal, awarded to individuals who have made especially meritorious contributions to U.S. security, national interests, world peace, or significant public and private endeavors. "I am honored and humbled to receive the Presidential Medal of Freedom from my nation and from our Commander-in-Chief, President Donald J. Trump," Giuliani, 82, said in a statement. queue.dek: Meta is teaming up with Gopuff to let users order groceries and household essentials directly through AI chats with delivery in as little as 15 minutes.
queue.opening: Shoppers can now hand off their grocery lists to artificial intelligence — and have bags at their front doors in 15 minutes — without ever leaving a chat window. Instant commerce giant Gopuff and Meta unveiled a direct integration Tuesday that plugs Gopuff’s rapid delivery network straight into Muse, Meta’s personal AI agent, letting users turn casual prompts or saved social media recipes into real-world deliveries. The new partnership allows Muse users to browse, build and approve orders from a catalog of more than 5,000 fresh groceries and household essentials, with deliveries arriving as fast as 15 minutes. Rather than redirecting users to a separate retail app or website, the new integration plugs directly into Gopuff’s live inventory, pricing, promotions and delivery-time systems. queue.dek: U.S. defense officials are reportedly exploring deals with Detroit automakers and parts suppliers to mass-produce military drone components, though profit margins remain a hurdle.
queue.opening: The Pentagon is reportedly in preliminary talks with General Motors, Ford Motor Co. and other major manufacturers to help mass-produce military drones. Citing people familiar with the matter, The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that U.S. defense officials are exploring deals in which automakers and parts suppliers — including Canadian auto parts giant Magna International — would supply components such as motors, actuators and sensors to drone makers. However, no deals have been finalized, and executives have reportedly raised questions about profit margins and the business case for entering the weapons supply chain. FOX Business reached out to the Department of War, General Motors, Ford, Magna International and Lacks Enterprises for comment. queue.title: US Army to proceed with Iowa detonation of degraded bomb materials: ‘A consensus decision’
queue.dek: The Army will detonate 68 barrels of crystallized lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown after a federal appeals court ruling.
queue.opening: The U.S. Army will detonate 68 barrels of unstable, degraded bomb-making chemicals in Iowa on Wednesday morning after a federal appeals court rejected a legal challenge and allowed the controlled blast to move forward. In a statement late Monday, Army officials confirmed they are proceeding with destroying the crystallized lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown in coordination with state, local and federal authorities. "This is a consensus decision," Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle posted on social media. "Every expert agency agrees, and both Iowa’s current and incoming Governors say the call belongs to the experts."
